title: The 3 tricks hiding in most phishing emails
description: Phishing messages look different, but most lean on the same psychological levers. Learn them and you'll spot scams faster.

scenes.big: This email wants you to panic
scenes.say: That urgent email from your bank? It wants you to panic. Because panicking people don't stop to check things.
Phishing emails look different, but most reuse the same three tricks.
First, authority. It pretends to be someone important. Second, urgency. A tight deadline, or a threat. Third, emotion. Fear, excitement, or curiosity, anything to rush you.
Then there's the link. The text you see can say one thing, while the real address behind it says another. On a computer, hover over it to check before you click.
If something feels off, stop, and contact the company using details you already trust. Forward scam emails to report at phishing dot gov dot U K. Follow for the next one.
